correctness.rationale: For n≥2 and r≥1, the published Theorem 22 gives homology only in odd degree 2r-1. Under any rotation the augmented signed fixed-face trace reduces exactly to minus the signed independence sum of vertex-orbit choices. Orbit color subsets are empty, singleton, or multi-color; the weighted transfer matrix has characteristic polynomial (λ+1)^(n-1)(λ³-(n-1)). This proves the full trace for all rotation exponents and the dimension boundary, including d=1,2. Induced-word and 2-dimensional cubic/sign module characters reproduce every trace, proving the rational module decomposition. Burnside gives the invariant dimensions. Actual embedded verifier exhaustively checked signed simplex traces in six cases and transfer/module/Fourier properties in seven cases; these finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Theorem 22 in Antolín Camarena–Carnero Bravo (arXiv:2307.12401v1, 2023) classifies nonequivariant sphere wedges for precisely this graph family but does not derive nonidentity rotation traces, the positive word-induced cyclic module, or the necklace-count invariant rank. Goyal–Shukla–Singh (arXiv:1905.06926v1, Proposition 3.2) likewise provides complete-graph-product sphere counts only. Direct comparisons of domain, statement and implication with these relevant primary sources and indexed related studies did not identify a stronger or equivalent prior character classification. Novelty is best-knowledge, not proven uniqueness.

value.rationale: This is a full, natural two-parameter cyclic symmetry representation of the homology of an already important graph-product independence-complex family. Existing wedge multiplicities do not determine nonidentity rotation traces. The positive induced-module/necklace description is structural, explains an exact invariant dimension and a parity transition, and supplies information useful for studying symmetry quotients and refinements without requiring an equivariant homotopy equivalence. It is not a computed isolated small instance, arbitrary slice, or a direct reformulation of the known Betti rank.
